# The Starving Coding Academy

> A completely free, ad-free beginner course for learning how programming works before becoming attached to one language's syntax.

The academy teaches transferable programming concepts with examples from Python, JavaScript, Java, C#, C++ and Lua. It is designed for complete beginners and uses short lessons, comparisons, quick checks and small practice exercises.

The public website is https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/

The material is licensed under [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/). People may share and adapt it with attribution for noncommercial use, and adaptations must use the same license.

## Course facts

- The course contains 42 lessons.
- The curriculum begins with raw programming concepts, then covers syntax, values, operators, program structure, functions, objects, control flow, loops and cumulative practice.
- The lessons compare six languages without asking learners to memorize all six at once.
- Progress is stored locally in the learner's browser and can be exported as a human-readable JSON backup.
- The course is free, contains no advertisements and does not require an account.
- The site source is public on [GitHub](https://github.com/aylanj123/The-Starving-Coding-Academy).
- The community link is [The Starving Coding Academy Discord](https://discord.gg/KzPR9cRBgs).

## Lesson catalog

- [Raw programming concepts](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/raw-programming.html)
  - **Summary** — This course introduces values, decisions, repetition and program structure using examples from Python, JavaScript, Java, C#, C++ and Lua.
  - **Learning goals** — separate a programming concept from one language's spelling; recognize the common pieces inside a small program; choose a language because it fits a goal
  - **Key topics** — Programming concepts and syntax; Common parts of programs; Choosing a programming language; Raw programming lessons
  - **References** — [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/); [MDN JavaScript guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide); [Java language basics](https://dev.java/learn/language-basics/); [Lua 5.4 reference manual](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html)

- [What coding is used for](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/what-is-coding.html)
  - **Summary** — Coding means writing precise instructions for a computer. Those instructions also need to remain readable enough for people to understand, test and change.
  - **Learning goals** — explain the difference between a goal, an algorithm, and code; identify input, processing, and output; describe why humans are part of the audience for code
  - **Key topics** — Turning goals into instructions; Input processing and output; Code for computers and people
  - **References** — [Python tutorial introduction](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/introduction.html); [MDN JavaScript guide introduction](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Introduction)

- [Syntax rules and program meaning](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/syntax-rules.html)
  - **Summary** — Syntax is the grammar of a programming language. It defines how names, symbols and code structures must be arranged to form valid instructions.
  - **Learning goals** — distinguish syntax from program behavior; read a syntax error as location evidence; compare the same idea in several languages
  - **Key topics** — Why syntax rules matter; The same decision in different languages; Syntax and semantics
  - **References** — [Python lexical analysis](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html); [JavaScript lexical grammar](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Lexical_grammar); [Lua lexical conventions](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#3.1)

- [Types of programming failures](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/when-code-breaks.html)
  - **Summary** — Programming failures can happen before execution, while the program runs or after it produces a result. Error messages and incorrect results provide information about the cause.
  - **Learning goals** — classify common failure stages; use an error message without panicking; reduce a bug to a smaller experiment
  - **Key topics** — Computers follow literal instructions; When errors happen; First steps after finding an error; Choose the next tool
  - **References** — [Python errors and exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html); [MDN JavaScript error reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Error)

- [Debugging with evidence](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/errors-debugging.html)
  - **Summary** — Debugging is the process of forming a specific explanation for a problem, testing it with a small experiment and revising that explanation from the result.
  - **Learning goals** — write an expected-versus-actual bug report; trace values through a program; choose a debugging tool that fits the symptom
  - **Key topics** — Build a useful bug report; Debugging tools; Follow the data
  - **References** — [MDN console API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/console); [Chrome DevTools JavaScript debugging](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/javascript); [Visual Studio Code debugging](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/debugtest/debugging)

- [Exceptions and error recovery](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/exceptions-recovery.html)
  - **Summary** — An exception reports a problem that occurred while a program was running. It can move through the call stack until code handles it or the program stops.
  - **Learning goals** — trace an exception through active function calls; choose between recovery and propagation; keep cleanup dependable while preserving useful error context
  - **Key topics** — How exceptions change control flow; Exception handlers and recovery; Catching specific exceptions; Exception handling across languages; Cleanup after success or failure; Common exception handling mistakes
  - **References** — [Python errors and exceptions](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html); [Java exceptions](https://dev.java/learn/exceptions/); [C# exceptions and exception handling](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/exceptions/); [Lua error handling](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#2.3)

- [Starting a program](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/starting-project.html)
  - **Summary** — A program begins when an environment loads its code and calls an entry point. Frameworks may begin execution through lifecycle functions that respond to events.
  - **Learning goals** — identify an entry point; distinguish source code from the runtime that executes it; start a tiny project without drowning in setup
  - **Key topics** — Source code tools and runtime; Entry points across languages; The first program goal
  - **References** — [Python interpreter](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/interpreter.html); [Java getting started](https://dev.java/learn/getting-started/); [C# program structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/program-structure/)

- [Basic syntax elements](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/syntax-elements.html)
  - **Summary** — Expressions and statements are built from names, literals, keywords, operators, punctuation and comments. Each element has a specific role in the instruction.
  - **Learning goals** — label common syntax elements; separate an expression from a statement; read punctuation according to context
  - **Key topics** — From characters to programs; Expressions produce values; Punctuation in code; Syntax lessons
  - **References** — [Python lexical analysis](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html); [JavaScript grammar and types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Grammar_and_types); [Lua lexical conventions](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#3.1)

- [Variables and assignment](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/values-variables.html)
  - **Summary** — A variable gives a value a name so the program can use it later. Its declaration determines whether another value can replace it.
  - **Learning goals** — distinguish a variable from its current value; name state according to its purpose; trace assignment from right to left
  - **Key topics** — Names and values; Variable naming; Declaration initialization and reassignment
  - **References** — [Python assignment statements](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#assignment-statements); [JavaScript let](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/let); [C# variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/language-specification/variables)

- [Writing useful comments](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/comments.html)
  - **Summary** — Comments are notes for people reading the source code. The language ignores them during execution, so they can explain decisions and context that the code does not show clearly.
  - **Learning goals** — write a useful reason-focused comment; recognize common comment syntax; avoid using comments to rescue confusing code
  - **Key topics** — Comment syntax differs; What useful comments explain; Removing outdated comments
  - **References** — [Python comments](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#comments); [JavaScript comments](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Lexical_grammar#comments); [Java comments](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se25/html/jls-3.html#jls-3.7)

- [Basic value types](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/primitive-values.html)
  - **Summary** — Programming languages provide basic value categories for numbers, text, booleans and absence. A category may be primitive in one language and an object or special value in another.
  - **Learning goals** — choose a suitable basic type for a value; explain why numeric types are not interchangeable; recognize values that represent absence
  - **Key topics** — Common basic value categories; Operations depend on type; Numbers have limits
  - **References** — [Python built-in types](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html); [JavaScript data types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Data_structures); [Java primitive data types](https://dev.java/learn/language-basics/primitive-types/); [C# built-in types](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/built-in-types)

- [How type systems interpret values](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/strong-typing.html)
  - **Summary** — A type tells the language how to interpret a value and which operations are allowed. Type rules prevent incompatible values from being combined accidentally.
  - **Learning goals** — picture how a type gives stored data meaning; explain why stricter type rules can prevent bugs; predict whether a mixed-type mistake fails early or while running
  - **Key topics** — Values need types; Values and references; Benefits of stricter type checks; Type errors across languages; Explicit type conversion; Comparing type systems
  - **References** — [Python data model](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html); [JavaScript data types](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Data_structures); [C# type system](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/types/)

- [Complex data types](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/complex-types.html)
  - **Summary** — Complex types combine multiple values or behaviors into one structure. Collections, records, objects and functions provide different ways to organize that information.
  - **Learning goals** — choose between a sequence and a key-value structure; describe value versus reference behavior cautiously; recognize functions as values where supported
  - **Key topics** — Choosing a data structure; Similar data structures across languages; Shared references to one object
  - **References** — [Python data structures](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/datastructures.html); [JavaScript keyed collections](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Keyed_collections); [Lua tables](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#2.1)

- [Boolean values and conditions](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/booleans.html)
  - **Summary** — A boolean stores one of two logical values, usually true or false . Programs use booleans in decisions, loops, validation, filters and permissions.
  - **Learning goals** — phrase boolean names as questions; build booleans from comparisons; predict simple truth-table results
  - **Key topics** — Stored and calculated booleans; Comparisons create booleans; Combining boolean expressions
  - **References** — [Python truth-value testing](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#truth-value-testing); [JavaScript Boolean](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Boolean); [C# Boolean type](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/bool)

- [Operators and operands](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/operators.html)
  - **Summary** — Operators calculate, compare, combine, assign or transform values. Each operator works with one or more operands, and its exact behavior depends on the language and operand types.
  - **Learning goals** — identify unary, binary, and assignment operators; use precedence without relying on memory; check language-specific operator behavior
  - **Key topics** — Operators act on operands; Operator categories; Operator precedence and grouping; Operator behavior by type
  - **References** — [Python expressions](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html); [JavaScript operators](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Expressions_and_operators); [Java operators](https://dev.java/learn/language-basics/using-operators/)

- [Joining and formatting strings](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/string-concatenation.html)
  - **Summary** — String concatenation joins pieces of text. Interpolation inserts values into a text template, while formatting controls how those values appear.
  - **Learning goals** — distinguish numeric addition from text joining; use interpolation for readable messages; avoid accidental coercion
  - **Key topics** — Text concatenation rules; String interpolation; Formatting values
  - **References** — [Python formatted string literals](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html#f-strings); [JavaScript template literals](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Template_literals); [Java String formatted](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/String.html#formatted(java.lang.Object...)); [Lua string.format](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#pdf-string.format)

- [Arithmetic in programming](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/mathematical-operators.html)
  - **Summary** — Programming arithmetic includes addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, remainders and exponentiation. Operand types, numeric limits and language rules affect the result.
  - **Learning goals** — use remainder for repeating patterns; predict grouping with precedence; spot division and precision traps
  - **Key topics** — Basic arithmetic operators; Remainders and repeating ranges; Division follows type rules
  - **References** — [Python arithmetic conversions](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#binary-arithmetic-operations); [JavaScript arithmetic operators](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators#arithmetic_operators); [C# arithmetic operators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/operators/arithmetic-operators)

- [Boolean logic](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/logical-operators.html)
  - **Summary** — Logical operators combine or invert boolean conditions. AND , OR and NOT express how several conditions belong together.
  - **Learning goals** — translate a sentence into a boolean expression; explain short-circuit evaluation; simplify confusing negative logic
  - **Key topics** — Translating rules into boolean expressions; Short-circuiting prevents unsafe checks; Naming boolean conditions
  - **References** — [Python Boolean operations](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#boolean-operations); [JavaScript logical operators](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators#binary_logical_operators); [C# Boolean logical operators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/operators/boolean-logical-operators)

- [Shorthand assignment and increment operators](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/shorthand-operators.html)
  - **Summary** — Shorthand operators update an existing value with less code. Common forms include compound assignment and the increment operators available in some languages.
  - **Learning goals** — expand compound assignment mentally; recognize language differences around increment; avoid clever state changes inside larger expressions
  - **Key topics** — Compound assignment; Increment operators across languages; Clear state changes
  - **References** — [JavaScript assignment operators](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators#assignment_operators); [JavaScript increment operator](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Increment); [C# arithmetic operators](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/operators/arithmetic-operators)

- [Program input and output](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/input-output.html)
  - **Summary** — Input is information received by a program, and output is information the program produces. Both can move through keyboards, screens, files, controllers, databases or networks.
  - **Learning goals** — identify input and output beyond the console; validate untrusted input; separate core logic from interface code
  - **Key topics** — Types of input and output; Validate outside data before using it; Separating input from logic; Designing useful output
  - **References** — [Python input and output](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/inputoutput.html); [MDN client-side form validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Forms/Form_validation); [MDN constraint validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Constraint_validation)

- [Organizing code](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/code-structure.html)
  - **Summary** — Program structure organizes code into blocks, functions, objects and modules. Each level groups related instructions, behavior or data.
  - **Learning goals** — recognize common levels of code organization; explain cohesion and coupling in plain language; choose the next useful boundary
  - **Key topics** — Levels of code structure; Organizing by responsibility; Code structure lessons
  - **References** — [Python modules](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/modules.html); [JavaScript modules](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules); [Java packages](https://dev.java/learn/packages/)

- [Scope and visibility](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/scope-code-blocks.html)
  - **Summary** — A code block groups instructions, while a scope defines where a declared name can be used. Languages differ in how blocks create or affect scopes.
  - **Learning goals** — trace a name to its declaration; explain local versus wider scope; avoid accidental shadowing and leaked state
  - **Key topics** — Local and outer scope; Block syntax by language; Variable shadowing
  - **References** — [Python scopes and namespaces](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/classes.html#python-scopes-and-namespaces); [JavaScript scope](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Scope); [C# declaration spaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/language-specification/basic-concepts#declarations)

- [Defining and calling functions](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/functions.html)
  - **Summary** — A function gives a block of behavior a name. It can receive inputs, perform an operation and return a result to the caller.
  - **Learning goals** — describe a function's contract; separate calling from defining; choose a focused function responsibility
  - **Key topics** — Definition versus call; Function inputs outputs and effects; Matching behavior to a function name; Function lessons
  - **References** — [Python defining functions](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/controlflow.html#defining-functions); [JavaScript functions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Functions); [Java methods](https://dev.java/learn/classes-objects/defining-methods/)

- [Parameters arguments and default values](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/parameters-arguments.html)
  - **Summary** — Parameters define the inputs a function accepts. Arguments are the values supplied for those parameters when the function is called, and default values can make some inputs optional.
  - **Learning goals** — use parameter and argument precisely; recognize when an optional parameter may be omitted; recognize when several settings may belong in an object
  - **Key topics** — Required and optional parameters; Configuration objects group related settings; Passing values and references
  - **References** — [Python default argument values](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/controlflow.html#default-argument-values); [JavaScript default parameters](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Functions/Default_parameters); [C# named and optional arguments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/classes-and-structs/named-and-optional-arguments)

- [Returning values from functions](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/return-values.html)
  - **Summary** — A return value sends a result from a function back to its caller. A function can also return early when a requirement fails or its work is already complete.
  - **Learning goals** — capture and use returned values; distinguish return from print; use guard clauses responsibly
  - **Key topics** — Printing and returning; Return exits the current function; Returning result objects
  - **References** — [Python return statements](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-return-statement); [JavaScript return](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/return); [C# return statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/jump-statements#the-return-statement)

- [Anonymous functions and callbacks](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/lambdas.html)
  - **Summary** — A lambda defines an anonymous function inside an expression. Lambdas commonly provide short callbacks for sorting, filtering and event handling.
  - **Learning goals** — recognize anonymous function syntax; explain a callback; know when to replace a lambda with a named function
  - **Key topics** — Functions as values; Callbacks for sorting and filtering; When to use a lambda
  - **References** — [Python lambda expressions](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#lambda); [JavaScript arrow functions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Functions/Arrow_functions); [JavaScript closures](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Closures)

- [Classes objects and instances](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/objects.html)
  - **Summary** — An object groups data with operations that use or change that data. In class-based languages, a class defines the fields and methods available to its instances.
  - **Learning goals** — distinguish a class from an instance; group related state and behavior; recognize object identity and relationships
  - **Key topics** — Classes and instances; What an object contains; When to use objects; Object lessons
  - **References** — [Python classes](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/classes.html); [JavaScript classes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes); [Java classes and objects](https://dev.java/learn/classes-objects/)

- [Object fields and state](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/fields.html)
  - **Summary** — Fields store information that belongs to an object or type. Languages may call them fields, attributes, properties or data members and provide different access rules for them.
  - **Learning goals** — recognize instance and class/static state; explain encapsulation; avoid exposing mutable internals carelessly
  - **Key topics** — Instance fields; Static and shared fields; Field access and encapsulation
  - **References** — [Java fields](https://dev.java/learn/classes-objects/creating-classes/); [JavaScript public class fields](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Classes/Public_class_fields); [C# fields](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/classes-and-structs/fields)

- [Object methods](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/methods.html)
  - **Summary** — A method is a function attached to an object or type. Instance methods use a particular object's state, while static or class methods belong to the type itself.
  - **Learning goals** — distinguish method calls from property access; choose instance or static behavior; write methods that preserve object rules
  - **Key topics** — Method receivers; Queries and commands; Methods that update related state
  - **References** — [Java methods](https://dev.java/learn/classes-objects/defining-methods/); [JavaScript method definitions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Functions/Method_definitions); [C# methods](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/methods)

- [Dot notation and member access](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/dot-notation.html)
  - **Summary** — Dot notation selects a named member from an object, type, namespace or module. It can access a field, select a method or continue through a chain of members.
  - **Learning goals** — read a dotted expression left to right; distinguish selection from invocation; debug a broken member chain
  - **Key topics** — Selecting and calling a method; Reading a member chain; Namespaces and modules
  - **References** — [JavaScript property accessors](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Property_accessors); [Python attribute references](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#attribute-references); [C# member access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/operators/member-access-operators)

- [Uses of parentheses](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/parentheses.html)
  - **Summary** — Parentheses group expressions, call functions, define parameters and surround conditions in some languages. Their role depends on the syntax around them.
  - **Learning goals** — identify common parenthesis roles; use grouping for clarity; avoid confusing a function value with a function call
  - **Key topics** — Common uses of parentheses; Function reference or function call; Calls without arguments
  - **References** — [Python calls](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#calls); [JavaScript functions and calls](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Functions); [JavaScript grouping operator](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Grouping)

- [Control flow and execution order](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/control-flow.html)
  - **Summary** — Control flow determines which statement a program executes next. Branches choose a path, loops repeat a block and transfers such as return leave the current path.
  - **Learning goals** — trace execution through a branch or loop; choose between selection and repetition; recognize transfers such as return, break, and continue
  - **Key topics** — Types of control flow; Tracing execution; Choosing a control structure
  - **References** — [Python control flow tools](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/controlflow.html); [JavaScript control flow](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Control_flow_and_error_handling); [Java control flow](https://dev.java/learn/language-basics/controlling-flow/)

- [If else and else if branches](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/if-else.html)
  - **Summary** — An if chain checks conditions in order and runs the first matching branch. The order matters when several conditions can be true for the same value.
  - **Learning goals** — trace first-match behavior; order overlapping conditions; choose independent if statements versus one chain
  - **Key topics** — One branch from an if chain; Separate if statements; Guard clauses and early returns
  - **References** — [Python if statements](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/compound_stmts.html#the-if-statement); [JavaScript if...else](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/if...else); [C# if statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/selection-statements#the-if-statement)

- [Loop fundamentals](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/loops.html)
  - **Summary** — A loop repeats a block while a condition remains true or while items remain to process. Its condition and changing state determine when repetition stops.
  - **Learning goals** — identify initialization, condition, update, and body; choose a condition-driven or collection-driven loop; prevent common infinite loops
  - **Key topics** — Parts of a loop; Choosing a loop type; Break and continue
  - **References** — [Python for and while statements](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/compound_stmts.html#the-while-statement); [JavaScript loops and iteration](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Loops_and_iteration); [Java loop statements](https://dev.java/learn/language-basics/controlling-flow/#looping)

- [While loops](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/while-loops.html)
  - **Summary** — A while loop checks its condition before every iteration and repeats while that condition is true. It can run zero times when the first check is false.
  - **Learning goals** — predict zero-iteration behavior; write a clear termination condition; add safety bounds to uncertain repetition
  - **Key topics** — Condition checked before each iteration; When to use a while loop; Ending a while loop
  - **References** — [Python while statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/compound_stmts.html#the-while-statement); [JavaScript while](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/while); [C# while statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/iteration-statements#the-while-statement)

- [Do while and repeat until loops](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/do-while.html)
  - **Summary** — A post-test loop checks its condition after running the body, so the body runs at least once. Languages provide forms such as do-while and repeat-until .
  - **Learning goals** — explain guaranteed first execution; translate between do-while and repeat-until; simulate a post-test loop when syntax is absent
  - **Key topics** — Validate numeric input; While and until conditions; Emulating do while in Python
  - **References** — [JavaScript do...while](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/do...while); [Lua repeat statement](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#3.3.4); [C# do statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/iteration-statements#the-do-statement)

- [For loops and ranges](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/for-loops.html)
  - **Summary** — A for loop repeats over a range, counter, iterator or sequence of values. Some languages use a three-part loop header, while others iterate directly over values.
  - **Learning goals** — trace start, condition, and update; avoid off-by-one errors; choose a range that matches the requirement
  - **Key topics** — C-style for loops; Python ranges and indexes; Lua ranges and indexes; Loop boundaries and off-by-one errors
  - **References** — [JavaScript for](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for); [Python range](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#range); [Lua for statement](https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/manual.html#3.3.5)

- [Foreach loops](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/foreach-loops.html)
  - **Summary** — A foreach loop processes each element in a collection without a manually updated index. Languages may spell this construct as for , foreach or enhanced for .
  - **Learning goals** — choose values over indexes when possible; distinguish JavaScript for...of from for...in; avoid mutating a collection unsafely during iteration
  - **Key topics** — Iterating directly over values; Iterating over keys values and indexes; Modifying collections during iteration
  - **References** — [JavaScript for...of](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for...of); [JavaScript Object.entries](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/entries); [Python enumerate](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#enumerate); [C# foreach statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/statements/iteration-statements#the-foreach-statement)

- [Switch statements and cases](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/switch-cases.html)
  - **Summary** — A switch compares one value with a set of cases and runs the matching case. Some languages also allow cases to match types, ranges, patterns or guard conditions.
  - **Learning goals** — choose switch versus if; understand fall-through risks; use a default case intentionally
  - **Key topics** — Matching one value against cases; Using fall-through on purpose; Choosing between switch and if; Switch syntax across languages
  - **References** — [JavaScript switch](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/switch); [Java switch expressions and statements](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/26/language/switch-expressions-statements.html); [C++ switch statement](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/cpp/switch-statement-cpp?view=msvc-170)

- [Programming practice and feedback](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/practice.html)
  - **Summary** — Programming practice includes predicting a result, writing a small solution, running it and comparing the output with the prediction. The difference identifies what needs further study.
  - **Learning goals** — practice without waiting for a giant project; turn mistakes into specific feedback; choose a challenge just beyond current comfort
  - **Key topics** — A short practice cycle; Types of practice; Make an exercise fit you; Practice lessons; What the final practice covers
  - **References** — [Python unittest](https://docs.python.org/3/library/unittest.html); [MDN debugging JavaScript](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Scripting/Debugging_JavaScript); [Visual Studio testing tools](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/test/?view=visualstudio)

- [Small complete programs](https://aylanj123.github.io/The-Starving-Coding-Academy/pages/tiny-examples.html)
  - **Summary** — These examples are complete programs designed for tracing and modification. Each one includes a prediction step and a small change to implement.
  - **Learning goals** — trace state and control flow; translate one concept between languages; extend a working program without rewriting it
  - **Key topics** — 01 · Damage calculator; 02 · Cooldown gate; 03 · Inventory search; 04 · Player health; 05 · Wrapped selection; 06 · Validate before using; 07 · Format a status line; 08 · Create independent settings; 09 · Follow a callback and closure; 10 · Build a menu boundary; 11 · Total usable durability
  - **References** — [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/); [MDN JavaScript guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide); [Java learning path](https://dev.java/learn/); [C# guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/)

  - **Summary** — This quiz checks the programming concepts covered throughout the course. Each question focuses on explaining behavior or predicting a result.
  - **Learning goals** — explain core concepts without memorized slogans; trace unfamiliar-looking examples; identify the next lesson worth revisiting
  - **Key topics** — Round 1 · Concepts; Round 2 · Trace operations; Concept check · Operators and text; Round 3 · Debug; Concept check · Debugging decisions; Round 4 · Design; Round 5 · Connect the lessons; Reviewing the results
